dedupe_keys.name: digripy district heating grid simulation in python

description: DiGriPy (District Heating Grid Simulation in Python) is an open simulation tool for district heating networks. It was released in June 2021 (version 1.0.0) by Lena Vorspel and Jens Bücker, with copyright held by the Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft, and a description and validation of the tool are given in their 2021 paper in the journal Computation. It installs with pip and runs from the command line on example scenarios, such as a medium-temperature network case, for a chosen number of time steps; results are displayed in a browser and saved as spreadsheets in a results folder. It uses the CoolProp property library, which the README notes needs Python older than 3.9. Coverage is not tied to a place. The code is accessible on GitHub and Zenodo under the MIT licence at no cost. Caveats: the last commit was in March 2022, and the Python version limit makes installation harder today. Simulation uses are thermal-hydraulic simulation of district heating operation and temperature reduction scenarios. Related records: model-dhnx covers district heating network optimisation, and data-opendhn-verbier-meshed-district-heating-benchmark can be used for validation.
inputs: district heating network and scenario files
name: DiGriPy - District Heating Grid Simulation in Python
